title: Cutover orchestration safety matrix and preflight notes
content:
TL;DR:
A compact working draft outlining a safety-first cutover and upgrade orchestration approach for private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. Focus: zero‑surprise API compatibility, terraform module pin/upgrade pattern, canary routing + traffic mirroring, fast rollback paths, cache warmup, and post-cut validation checks. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — checklist + safety matrix + open questions for SEs and SREs to iterate on.

Scope and intent:
- Target: private-controlplane + serving-runtime upgrades where customers run Redwood Private in VPC or on-prem appliance.
- Includes: terraform module lifecycle strategy, API shim generation, compatibility guards, rollout orchestration, rollback fast paths, and observability gating.
- Excludes: long-term migration of legacy customer config formats (separate tracked task).

Goals:
- Keep production customer endpoints available (SLO: 99.9% per-customer) during staged upgrades.
- Minimize blast radius; automated fallbacks for API incompatibility and capacity regressions.
- Reduce operator cognitive load: clear preflight checks, automated contract tests, and a single-command rollback path.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting existing terraform modules — this doc assumes small, additive changes and a compatibility shim approach.
- Database schema redesigns — only coordination patterns for quiescing/reads/writes covered.

Preconditions (hard gates before any cutover):
1) Schema/contract tests green for the current->candidate control plane APIs (see contract-test-runner).
2) Terraform module pins for modules used by customer installs are enumerated and approved in PRs.
3) Canary infra (subset VPC or isolated on-prem blade) provisioned and accessible.
4) Runbook owner and oncall SRE assigned for the window and a backout owner for rollback.

Terraform module strategy (practical rules):
- Semantic upgrades: annotate modules with a compatibility tag (major.minor.compat). Sequence: patch -> minor (compat) -> major (breaking).
- Use a "two-tag" release pattern for private modules: stable-tag (customer-locked) + rollout-tag (temporary). Example: rmodule-gpu/1.3.2@stable, rmodule-gpu/1.4.0@rollout-2025-09-xx.
- PR checklist for module upgrade: upgrade guides entry, smoke TF plan artifacts uploaded to PR, label: private-deploy-upgrade, automated plan in staging env.
- Terraform drift detection preflight: run plan against an inventory of customer TF states (internal script) and fail if >5% of states report unexpected diffs.

API shim + contract compatibility pattern:
- For any change to HTTP/GRPC endpoints, auto-generate a shim layer that maps old requests -> new request shape. Place shim beside control plane router; shim enabled by default in candidate but configurable by toggle.
- Contract tests: two flavors
  - Unit-level schema checks (fast): JSON schemas, protobuf descriptors.
  - End-to-end smoke harness (slower): runs canned scenarios against a canary control plane and a downstream serving-runtime replica.
- Merge gating: PR must include both test types. If any end-to-end scenario fails, abort rollout.

Canary & traffic strategy (safety matrix):
- Phase 0: Dry run. Deploy candidate control plane to canary cluster. Run internal synthetic load (low QPS) and functional checks.
- Phase 1: Traffic mirror + dark launch. Mirror 10% of production traffic to canary (no responses returned to clients). Monitor error spikes, latency distributions, and memory/KV pressure. Duration: 60–120 minutes.
- Phase 2: Live canary serving. Shift 1–5 small customers (low risk) to candidate via routing policy. Measure: 95/99 latency, error rate, token cost drift, and qualitative output diffs (eval set).
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp. If stable for 2 hours, ramp to 25% customer weight, then 50% with 15m hold, then full roll (each step with observability gates).
- Safety kills: automatic rollback trigger when any of: error rate > baseline + 1% absolute, p99 latency regresses > 2x, cache pressure causes evictions > threshold, or eval-quality delta exceeds configured threshold.

Traffic mirroring details:
- Prefer sidecar-level mirroring (transparent) where possible. Otherwise use proxy-level mirror (envoy/nginx) configured in the control plane router.
- Mirror sampling: deterministic hashing + header tag to ensure identical path selection and deterministic KV cache warmups.

KV cache warmup and cold-start mitigation:
- Warmup plan: use historical request prefixes (stored in curated snapshot) and replay against canary serving-runtime to populate KV caches before switching traffic.
- Warmup timeline: parallel to Phase 0; should complete before Phase 2. Include metrics: cache-hit-rate baseline vs candidate after warmup.

Stateful migrations and DB considerations:
- Prefer online-safe migrations (additive first). Strategy: dual-write (candidate + current) for new fields, read-fallback logic in shim.
- Quiesce plan for destructive migrations: schedule maintenance window; provide opt-in offline migration for customers requiring it.
- Snapshot and verification: take logical backups + verify checksums. Keep at least 3 retained copies across independent storage classes.

Rollback fast-paths and backout plan:
- Two rollback types:
  1) Soft rollback: routing change only (repoint traffic back to previous control plane). Time: minutes.
  2) Hard rollback: module/state reversion (terraform apply using pinned stable-tag). Time: hours.
- Fast rollbacks should be automated: operator runs single script (rollback.sh --customer <id>|--all) which performs routing revert, levies rate-limit holds, and triggers a focused smoke check.
- Post-rollback verification: confirm per-customer SLOs, DB consistency checks, KV cache stabilization.

Observability and gating metrics (minimum set):
- Per-customer error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (tokens), CPU/GPU utilization, memory/KV evictions, token cost per request, request-to-response correctness diff (eval set).
- Health probes: liveness + readiness + a compatibility probe that exercises common API paths.
- Alert rules: auto page on any production canary showing: sustained error spike, p99 regression, or memory OOM events.

Runbook checklist (preflight):
- [ ] Confirm backups: control plane configs, DB snapshots, TF state copies.
- [ ] Verify canary infra and access keys.
- [ ] Generate and run contract test suite against candidate.
- [ ] Create terraform rollout PRs and push rollout-tags.
- [ ] Prepare warmup dataset and run cache warmup job.
- [ ] Schedule windows, assign owners and rollback owner.
- [ ] Communicate with affected customers (if any).

During cutover: operator steps (short):
1. Deploy candidate to canary cluster.
2. Run synthetic smoke + contract tests.
3. Mirror traffic for 60–120m. If stable, proceed.
4. Move 1–5 small customers to live canary. Monitor 15–30m.
5. Ramp by policy with holds and automated gates.
6. If gate fails, trigger soft rollback script. If soft rollback fails to stabilize, escalate to hard rollback.

Post-cut validation queries and quick checks:
- Spot-check trace IDs across router -> control plane -> runtime to confirm request path unchanged.
- Run evaluation prompt set against both old and new models (or runtime) and compute a small set of difference metrics (BLEU-ish, token-length delta, hallucination heuristics).
- Confirm terraform state versions: for each module, record rollout-tag -> stable-tag mapping in deploy audit.

Open questions (needs engineering decisions):
- Should we require a mandatory API compatibility shim for every minor bump, or only for APIS flagged as "customer-facing"? (tradeoff: safety vs. code churn).
- Backpressure strategy: how aggressive should autoscaling be during canary mirroring? We currently risk double capacity usage (mirror + production). Need cost cap guard.
- Do we allow customers to opt out of auto rollback? (some customers prefer to remain on candidate longer for custom reasons).

Action items (next steps):
- Aisha: draft the rollback.sh prototype and add to infra repo (INF-2345).
- Marcus: add terraform tag enforcement to module release pipeline; add plan artifact upload step.
- Sofia: implement contract-test-runner job that posts results to PR and to canary dashboard.
- Ravi: prototype warmup replay job and measure cache hit improvement on a staging case.

Appendix / quick references:
- Minimal smoke test checklist (scripts/smoke): control-plane-health, api-contract, sample-end-to-end-run.
- Helpful tickets: INF-2345 (this effort), INF-2410 (warmup job), INF-2150 (module tagging).

Notes and meta:
- This is a working doc — expect iterations. Keep the rollout small, conservative, and reversible. Add any customer-specific bespoke steps to their install artifact rather than the core flow.
- Timestamp: notes compiled 2025-09-15; last edit 2025-10-02 by Aisha (outlines rollback.sh prototype approach and question list).
